positioning: MMIR is the orchestration layer for trusted AI: an AI control plane across local, edge, self-hosted and managed AI systems.
public_repo_rule: inkognitroz.github.io is public. It may contain static UI, public-safe manifests and non-sensitive local metadata only. Secrets, provider keys, billing, private user data and managed routing policy belong in private/protected backend or local connector repos.
principles: Not a chatbot, Ollama wrapper, local frontend or OpenAI clone
One perfect first local AI experience before marketplace, training, mesh economy or billing
Orchestration is the core product strength
No hidden paid routes or surprise spend

journeys.name: First useful answer
journeys.user_goal: Ask MMIR something immediately and get a helpful answer before setup.
journeys.trust_boundary: Public browser only. No backend, no account, no provider key.
journeys.free_first: Free browser guide route. No paid service.
steps: Page loads and prepares safe defaults automatically
Supergenious is selected when no live model is available
User types a prompt
Browser guide answers truthfully and explains next setup steps
journeys.done_when: A new visitor can send a prompt and receive an immediate response without choosing or configuring anything.
journeys.current_gap: Guide is deterministic, not a full LLM. WebGPU or local-node path is needed for real model reasoning.

journeys.name: First magical local AI activation
journeys.user_goal: Open mmir.ai, connect local AI, install, see own models and chat instantly.
journeys.trust_boundary: Browser to paired MMIR Local Node on 127.0.0.1, then to Ollama/local runtime.
journeys.free_first: Uses user's machine and free/open local models. No cloud spend.
steps: User opens mmir.ai
User chooses Connect local AI
MMIR shows the right one-file installer path for the user's device
Installer prepares MMIR Local Node and Ollama/model where possible while hiding brew, npm, Node.js, CORS, Docker and Terraform
Browser pairs with local node
Model discovery moves user's own models from installable to live
User chats instantly through /chat/completions
journeys.done_when: A normal user can open mmir.ai, click Connect local AI, install one file, return to MMIR, see local models and chat without reading architecture docs.
journeys.current_gap: Needs smoother DMG/PKG-level Mac install UX, stronger post-install detection, Windows/Linux parity and secure cross-device control-plane pairing beyond localhost.

journeys.name: Existing trusted backend
journeys.user_goal: Connect an already-owned local, self-hosted or OpenAI-compatible backend.
journeys.trust_boundary: Browser to explicit user-selected backend URL. Provider secrets must stay server-side.
journeys.free_first: Allowed by default only when route is local, free or self-hosted.
steps: User creates or edits backend profile
Public UI stores only metadata and key reference labels
Health/models are checked
Chat uses shared MMIR/OpenAI-compatible contract
journeys.done_when: Compatible backend can be selected, health checked, listed and used without exposing secrets in the public repo.
journeys.current_gap: More adapter-specific validation and guided setup is needed for non-local backends.

journeys.name: Model-agnostic orchestration
journeys.user_goal: Use MMIR as the orchestration layer above models: switch, route, compare, apply roles and synthesize.
journeys.trust_boundary: Browser orchestration over active trusted backend/local node. No hidden provider calls.
journeys.free_first: Works with free browser guide/local/self-hosted models first.
steps: User chooses a role or model
User sends task once
MMIR routes to selected model or compares multiple selected models
Responses are labeled by model/role
User can synthesize results
journeys.done_when: A user can see clearly which model/role answered, why it was routed there, and can switch, compare and synthesize without losing context.
journeys.current_gap: Comparison/synthesis needs more end-to-end smoke coverage and clearer first-screen discovery.

journeys.name: Workspace memory and knowledge
journeys.user_goal: Keep project context, preferences and uploaded knowledge available across tasks.
journeys.trust_boundary: Local browser storage by default; protected backend only when connected.
journeys.free_first: Local storage and file-backed backend options before paid databases.
steps: User creates/selects workspace
User adds memory or uploads knowledge
MMIR retrieves relevant context
User can inspect, export or delete local data
journeys.done_when: Context improves answers and the user can inspect/delete/export stored data.
journeys.current_gap: RAG and connector sync need stronger protected-backend coverage before enterprise claims.

journeys.name: Workflow orchestration
journeys.user_goal: Chain prompts, roles, tools, policies and actions into reusable AI workflows that matter more than chat.
journeys.trust_boundary: Workflow definitions in browser/protected backend; execution bounded by policy.
journeys.free_first: Manual and planning-only flows first. No paid automation by default.
steps: User defines workflow steps
MMIR validates inputs and execution policy
User runs or plans workflow
Results and gate status are visible
journeys.done_when: A workflow can be created, validated and run or safely planned with transparent gates.
journeys.current_gap: Needs more real execution paths, audit trail and workflow-level tests.

journeys.name: Progress and operator dashboard
journeys.user_goal: Follow what is shipped, beta, next, blocked and owned by which repo.
steps: Dashboard manifest is generated from backlog
User sees shipped/beta/next/watch/planned status
User sees repo ownership and decisions
Smoke test guards the manifest
journeys.done_when: Owner can follow progress without reading private repos or asking Codex for a manual status dump.
journeys.current_gap: Could later ingest GitHub Issues/PRs through protected tooling, but current public view is static-safe.

journeys.name: Managed API and provider routing
journeys.user_goal: Use hosted providers and managed routes safely through MMIR.
journeys.trust_boundary: Browser to protected API, then server-side vault/provider adapters.
journeys.free_first: Blocked from execution until identity, rate limit, audit and cost policy exist.
steps: User authenticates
Provider key is stored only server-side
Route policy checks identity, cost and permission
Provider adapter executes request
Audit logs event without raw prompt leakage
journeys.done_when: No key reaches public assets/localStorage, paid usage requires explicit approval, and route is auditable.
journeys.current_gap: Identity, secret vault and paid-route policy must be completed before launch.

journeys.name: Trusted node orchestration mesh
journeys.user_goal: Register trusted local/remote nodes and route work by capability, health, trust and cost.
journeys.trust_boundary: Protected API plus paired nodes with identity and policy.
journeys.free_first: Start with user-owned nodes and no anonymous compute.
steps: User installs a local/edge node on PC, VM, Raspberry Pi or Linux ARM device
Node registers with identity
MMIR records capabilities and health
Router chooses eligible node/model by policy
User sees why route was selected
journeys.done_when: Trusted nodes have identity, health, capabilities and policy-bound routing.
journeys.current_gap: Requires managed identity, node registry and routing policy hardening.
journeys.cost: zero for owned nodes; cloud spend blocked

journeys.name: Marketplace and premium orchestration
journeys.user_goal: Publish, share, buy or monetize models, workflows, agents and managed compute.
journeys.trust_boundary: Protected marketplace API with ownership, moderation, billing and policy.
journeys.free_first: Free product must work before marketplace monetization.
steps: Seller/provider registers listing
MMIR verifies trust, ownership and policy
User chooses listing with explicit cost
Execution happens through protected routing
journeys.done_when: Marketplace listings cannot expose secrets, misrepresent trust or charge without explicit user approval.
journeys.current_gap: Needs product validation, governance, payments and moderation before implementation.
